headline: US Nonfarm Payrolls Rise by 165,000 in October, Unemployment Falls to 4.1%
summary: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, surpassing the estimated 65,000. The unemployment rate unexpectedly declined to 4.1% following a soft September.
why: Employment data is a primary indicator of macroeconomic health and heavily influences Federal Reserve monetary policy decisions.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Stronger than expected job growth indicates robust economic activity in the United States.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The stronger-than-expected job additions and drop in unemployment signal a resilient labor market, beating consensus forecasts by a wide margin.
